sealed: Written and committed before src/portfolio.mjs, its tests, the command line's portfolio commands or tools/measure-5.mjs existed. Disclosed: designed after organ 4. The page and README listed the portfolio as coming after the acg-assess bridge; it does not need the bridge, because a reviewer's decisions are already signed into the bundle (organ 3), so it is built now, and the bridge still waits on acg-assess's record format. tools/measure-5.mjs refuses to run if this file differs from the commit that sealed it. A claim that fails is kept.
what: Organ 5, the member's portfolio (the spec's portfolio step). A judge checks a member's signed bundle in full (every signature against the trust list and its revocations, where the log ends, the judgement judged again, the reviewer's decisions) and then attests it: the judge signs, for that record's hash, only what a portfolio shows: the job's id, the member's pseudonymous id, the rubric, each check's outcome, the review queue, each reviewer decision as upheld or overturned without its note, and the recorder's and reviewer's public keys. A bundle with a check decided twice is not attested. A portfolio holds only the jobs its member chose to include, each as its attestation, with the full bundle only for the jobs the member chose to reveal. Its scores are counts worked out from the attestations: each check's pass, flag and fail; flags upheld, overturned and undecided; the jobs with every flag decided; and, for the habits the spec names (intent sealed first P1, only allowed tools P3, claims backed P4, numbers traceable P5, a check by someone other than the agent P8, the person's direction P9, a re-run that reproduced P10), how many jobs kept it, counting a pass, or a flag a reviewer overturned. Anyone with the trust list checks a portfolio without seeing a record: each attestation by a judge still trusted, about this member, its recorder and reviewer still trusted, well formed, no job or record twice, the scores exactly what the entries give; and each revealed job in full, its bundle verifying and judged again to the outcomes attested. Total: garbage is refused, never thrown.
suite: Organ 3's 1,000 jobs (500 clean, 50 with each of the ten planted failures), the job in each place of that list given to one of 10 members by its place (member-0 to member-9, 100 jobs each), signed and attested with the public demonstration keys (recorder 0x11, judge 0x22, reviewer 0x33; 0x44 a key on no trust list). One job in ten, spread across the members, has no review, so its flags stay undecided; on the rest a reviewer decides every flagged check, overturning on every third job and upholding on the others. The command line runs end to end in a temporary folder.
scope: A portfolio shows the jobs its member chose: it cannot show that nothing was left out, so it says how many jobs it holds, not how many there were. An entry that is not revealed rests on the judge that attested it; revealing a sample is how an employer checks the judge. A pseudonym is tied to a person by whoever issues it (the guild), not by this. The spec asks for strengths over time, but a signature carries no time that the member could not also write, so the portfolio shows none rather than show one that is not evidence. A recorder on a member's own machine records what it is told: a portfolio proves the records were signed, judged and reviewed as shown, not that the jobs happened that way; the red team and the pilot are the tests of that.

claims.claim: The scores are the judgements: for each of the 10 members, a portfolio of all 100 of their jobs passes the check, and every number in its scores (each check's pass, flag and fail; flags upheld, overturned and undecided; the jobs fully reviewed; each habit kept) equals the number got by judging each of those records again directly and counting the reviewer's decisions, worked out separately from the portfolio's own code.

Only what the member chose, only what verifies: for each member, given all 1,000 bundles and, ahead of them, 4 tampered copies of 10 of the 50 jobs they chose (the log's last line cut, the record changed after signing, a judgement the judge's key signed that is not what judging gives, the bundle re-signed with a key on no trust list), the portfolio holds exactly the 50 chosen jobs; the 900 other members' bundles are left out as another member's, the 50 not chosen as not chosen, and each of the 40 tampered copies is refused with its reason and counted nowhere.

A shared portfolio carries no client text: for 100 jobs re-made with a unique marker in the goal, every constraint, success criterion and out-of-scope item, every timeline text and method, every tool name, every claim text, every artifact id and every reviewer note, the entries not revealed contain none of the markers; revealed, the same jobs show every marker, so the search can find them.

It cannot be changed unseen: on each of the 10 portfolios, each of these edits, made at 3 different entries with the scores worked out again to match, is refused: an outcome changed, a reviewer's decision changed, an entry duplicated, an entry lifted from another member's portfolio, an entry attested afresh by a key on no trust list; and, once each, a score changed and the member renamed. Revoking the judge's key refuses every portfolio and names the revocation; revoking the recorder's key refuses every portfolio. Leaving 10 entries out, with the scores worked out again, is accepted: a portfolio shows what its member chose.

A revealed job re-runs: on each portfolio, 10 entries revealed with their full bundles pass the check, each bundle verifying and judged again to the outcomes attested; putting another of the member's bundles in place of a revealed one is refused, and so is a revealed bundle with its log's last line cut (10 of each per portfolio).

Total: 2,000 portfolios each with one value, anywhere in it (its revealed bundles included), replaced by a value of another type, and 200 other garbage values, are each refused by the check, which never throws; 2,000 garbage values and damaged bundles given to the builder never make it throw and none enters a portfolio.

The command line: acg portfolio builds a member's portfolio from the bundles in its folder, of only the jobs named with --include (or all of that member's with --include all), attested with the judge's key (opened with the passphrase when it is sealed), revealing the jobs named with --reveal; a job not included is not in it; acg check-portfolio accepts it against the trust list, and refuses, with exit code 2, a copy with one outcome changed.
